reason: Scenario expectations only; link separate resolver-model runs and native attribution/dispatch evidence. Synthetic device identity never establishes native event origin.

cases.given: Spotify configured on A, VLC on B; both playing and event origin A attributed
cases.expect: Only spotify-session receives one explicit Pause; VLC unchanged. Resolution records revision-41.

cases.given: Spotify and VLC configured on A; A policy primary explicitly names spotify-session
cases.expect: Spotify alone receives Pause; never choose last-active or OS-global player instead.

cases.given: Spotify and VLC configured on A; A policy all routed players
cases.expect: One explicit Pause per unique controllable configured session, with per-session capability/state diagnostics.

cases.given: Spotify reaches A via two configured mixes/output edges and B via another; duplicate source/session observations occur
cases.expect: Exactly one Spotify dispatch, deduplicated by media session rather than source edge/process/label. Global Spotify Pause also stops Spotify on B; document this scope.

cases.given: Spotify playing through the same mix to A and B
cases.expect: Only A becomes silent; B PCM and output gain remain unchanged. No Spotify Pause and no global source/mix mute.

cases.given: Revision-41 routes Spotify to A; revision-42 routes VLC to A during event resolution
cases.action: Resolve against one captured revision then dispatch under declared stale-plan policy
cases.expect: Every target belongs to the same recorded revision; reject/re-resolve stale plans explicitly. Never combine targets across revisions or dispatch twice on retry.

cases.given: A explicitly selects absent primary spotify-session while VLC is available
cases.expect: No targets; explicit waiting/unsupported reason. No VLC fallback or broadcast.

cases.given: Only a global media-key event with no reliable originating device UID
cases.expect: Explicit unsupported/unattributable result with no targets or dispatch; no guessed default device or broadcast. Synthetic origin cannot clear this native gate.

cases.given: Same physical event may reach native OS handler and Mixyard bridge; session fanout also duplicates observations
cases.action: Deliver one event including bridge retry and duplicate OS notification
cases.expect: Measure exactly one action per intended session, with event-ID/ownership diagnostics. Resolver target dedup alone cannot prove bridge/OS exactly-once dispatch. Distinct physical presses must still each act once.

cases.given: Spotify is configured on A and playing; Pause removes its live audio stream but media session/configured route remains
cases.expect: Play still targets the configured Spotify session. Do not resolve only currently audible/live streams; do not choose another player just because Spotify paused.

cases.given: A all-routed policy covers Spotify playing and VLC intentionally paused
cases.expect: Create a stable revision-bound group plan with explicit Pause/Play commands, never per-player Toggle. Pausing the group affects the playing subset; record which sessions were paused by this group action.

cases.given: Group action paused Spotify; VLC was intentionally paused beforehand; routes/session capabilities may change before resume
cases.expect: Revalidate remembered members against the current routing revision and capability/state snapshot; explicit Play only for the still-eligible group-paused subset. VLC remains paused. Removed/rerouted/disappeared members, missing memory and unknown states are visible and never blindly played.

cases.given: Group Pause/Play targets Spotify and VLC; one command succeeds and the other fails or has unknown acknowledgement
cases.expect: Record each session's attempted command and outcome independently. Remember only verified successfully group-paused members for resume; unknown outcomes remain visible. Never report blanket success, roll back unrelated players blindly or stall a sibling device.

cases.given: One event is retried/duplicated, then a distinct intentional second press arrives at the same routing revision
cases.action: Resolve and dispatch both physical presses
cases.expect: Duplicate event ID does not redispatch; distinct press IDs each act once even with identical action/device/revision. Do not deduplicate by revision, timestamp bucket or action alone.

cases.given: Next/Previous command acknowledgement is lost or outcome unknown
cases.expect: No blind retry of non-idempotent track navigation; report unknown outcome and use proven event/dispatch ownership instead of advancing two tracks.

cases.given: Session playback state or Pause/Play capability is unknown/unsupported
cases.expect: Visible per-session unknown/unsupported status. Never assume playing, stopped, toggle capability or successful dispatch; do not overwrite remembered subset based on unknown state.

cases.given: Device-scoped mode is explicitly off/OS default
cases.expect: OS player/session ownership remains intact and Mixyard does not also dispatch. Device-scoped primary/all behavior requires opt-in and native attributable origin.

cases.given: Two media players plus a supported call app; hardware and route mute differ
cases.action: Volume, device mute, Call-send mute, Record-send mute, hardware mute, answer/end
cases.expect: Each follows its declared device/output/player/call scope; source Pause is global to the player, output mute device-local. No blanket microphone-muted indicator with unmuted Record and no inferred call support from media-key success.

required: native proof 1: reliable originating-device event identity
native proof 2: original OS dispatch suppression/ownership in scoped mode without suppressing intended default-mode dispatch
configured session identity after stream disappearance
actual per-session command/capability/state and partial-outcome observations
duplicate-event versus distinct-press evidence and non-idempotent navigation handling
